# Pulse — Full Technical Guide

## 1. Summary

Pulse is a native macOS code editor written in Swift and AppKit. Its design constraint is memory: about 30 MB with several files open in CI measurements, a 50–60 MB target in normal use, and a hard limit of 100 MB enforced on every build. It uses no CPU while idle.

- Developer: Suraj Pisal
- License: MIT
- Platform: macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon and Intel
- Repository: https://github.com/Suraj1089/pulse
- Website: https://pulse0.app

Pulse 2.0 replaces the earlier Pulse menu-bar memory monitor (1.x), which remains available from GitHub Releases.

---

## 2. Features

- **Folders and files**: open a folder (⌘O), browse it in a sidebar file tree, open files in tabs. Folders are read only when expanded. New file, new folder, reveal in Finder, copy path and move to Trash from the tree's context menu.
- **Syntax highlighting**: Swift, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, C/C++/Objective-C, Java/Kotlin/Scala/Dart/C#, Ruby, shell, HTML/XML, CSS/SCSS, JSON, YAML, TOML, Markdown and SQL. Regex-based, not a full parser.
- **Editing**: line numbers, current-line highlight, auto-indent (including after `{`, `[`, `(` and Python `:`), spaces for tabs, toggle line comment (⌘/), indent and outdent (⌘] and ⌘[), word wrap (⌥⌘W), font size (⌘+, ⌘−, ⌘0).
- **Find and replace**: the standard macOS find bar (⌘F, ⌥⌘F, ⌘G, ⌘E).
- **Project search** (⇧⌘F): runs ripgrep (`rg`) as a short-lived child process when installed, otherwise a built-in scan. Results grouped by file; click to jump to the match.
- **Command palette**: ⌘P go to file (fuzzy), ⇧⌘P commands, ⌘L go to line.
- **Integrated terminal** (⌃`): your login shell via SwiftTerm, created on first use. Hiding the panel keeps the shell running; "Kill Terminal" ends it.
- **Autosave** (on by default): modified files with a path are written one second after typing stops, when Pulse loses focus, and at quit.
- **Session recovery**: the open folder, tabs, cursor positions and the text of unsaved buffers are stored in `~/Library/Application Support/Pulse/session.json` and restored at launch.
- **External changes**: files changed on disk are reloaded when Pulse regains focus, if they have no unsaved edits.
- **Resource meter**: the status bar shows Pulse's own physical footprint and CPU, and the footprint of shells it started, separately.

Not included by design: extensions, Git interface, debugger, language servers, AI features, telemetry, accounts.

---

## 3. Architecture

- **AppKit only.** No SwiftUI, no WKWebView, no storyboards. The only dependency is SwiftTerm for terminal emulation.
- **One text view for every tab.** Each document owns an `NSTextStorage` and an `UndoManager`. The editor has a single `NSLayoutManager` and `NSTextView`; switching tabs calls `replaceTextStorage`, so an open file costs roughly its own text.
- **TextKit 1** with non-contiguous layout, an `NSRulerView` gutter that draws only visible line numbers from a cached line index.
- **Highlighting** uses one combined `NSRegularExpression` per language and applies colors as layout-manager temporary attributes, which never modify or copy the text. Files up to 300 KB are highlighted in full, larger files around the visible range.
- **Laziness.** The terminal, the go-to-file index and folder contents are created on first use.
- **No idle work.** No polling or animations. The resource meter samples every 2 seconds only while Pulse is the active app.

---

## 4. Memory measurements

CI (`scripts/memory-check.sh`, GitHub macOS 14 runner) launches the bundled app and reads physical footprint with `vmmap --summary` after 8 seconds:

| Scenario | Pulse | Child processes |
|---|---|---|
| Empty window | 15.0 MB | 0 MB |
| Ten source files open | 31.8 MB | 0 MB |
| Ten files + terminal | 31.0 MB | 1.8 MB (shell) |

The build fails if Pulse exceeds 100 MB in any scenario. Numbers vary with display, font size, open files and macOS version.

---

## 5. Installation

One-line installer (downloads the latest release ZIP, installs to /Applications, clears quarantine, opens the app):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://pulse0.app/install.sh | bash
```

Disk image: https://github.com/Suraj1089/pulse/releases/latest/download/Pulse.dmg

From source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Suraj1089/pulse
cd pulse
swift run Pulse .          # run, opening the current folder
./scripts/bundle.sh        # build dist/Pulse.app
```

Open a folder from Terminal: `open -a Pulse .`

---

## 6. Keyboard shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| ⌘O | Open a folder or files |
| ⌘N | New file |
| ⌘S / ⇧⌘S / ⌥⌘S | Save / Save As / Save All |
| ⌘W | Close tab |
| ⌘P | Go to file |
| ⇧⌘P | Command palette |
| ⌘L | Go to line |
| ⌘F / ⌥⌘F | Find / Find and replace |
| ⇧⌘F | Search the project |
| ⇧⌘E | Show files |
| ⌃` | Show or hide the terminal |
| ⌘/ | Toggle line comment |
| ⌘] / ⌘[ | Indent / outdent |
| ⇧⌘] / ⇧⌘[ | Next / previous tab |
| ⌃⌘S | Toggle sidebar |
| ⌥⌘W | Word wrap |
| ⌘+ / ⌘− / ⌘0 | Font size |

---

## 7. Privacy

Pulse makes no network requests, has no telemetry or analytics, and needs no account. Files never leave the Mac.
